text:
ada: FYI ran into a nasty notebook + background auth refresher interaction when demoing the Python quickstart in Colab. Paste:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
# naive copy-paste from quickstart
resp = client.chat.completions.create(model="rwd-mini", input="hello")
print(resp.output_text)
```
I hit `RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop` at first, then after a kernel restart see `Task was destroyed but it is pending` and traceback into our auth refresher.

chris: yep we've seen this pattern. Notebooks have a running loop; our convenience helper currently calls `asyncio.run` and also eagerly spins up a background token refresher bound to that loop. When the kernel restarts the old loop disappears and the refresher tries to schedule on a closed loop -> ugly warnings/exceptions.

pat: quick repro steps I used: open Colab, run the quickstart cell, then use Runtime > Restart runtime, run the cell again. On 2/5 runs I get the destroyed-task warning; sometimes Colab shows an opaque `BrokenPipeError` instead.

sora: actionable proposals: 1) Docs: add a "Notebooks / Interactive shells" section in Quickstart with two patterns — an async example using `async with AsyncClient()` and a sync-safe helper for notebooks (or explicit warning). 2) SDK: make the sync helper detect running loop via `asyncio.get_running_loop()` and raise a clear RuntimeError that points to the notebook docs instead of calling `asyncio.run`. 3) Lifecycle: don't start auth refresher on import or when using sync helper; start it lazily and tie it to a loop that we manage so it can be closed cleanly. 4) Add a tiny helper `redwood.notebook.create_client()` that returns an AsyncClient properly wired for notebook lifecycles.

ada: +1. Also suggest a runtime debug-mode flag that, when enabled, turns the background refresher into a no-op in interactive envs to avoid noisy traces while prototyping.

chris: typed stubs note: editors in interactive windows were showing `create()` as returning Any, so folks don't see they need to await. We should fix the typing (pyi/stubs) so autocompletion suggests `await` and `async with`. That would cut down on these copy-paste mistakes.

pat: filed issue #2345: "Notebook Quickstart: AsyncClient, running event loop, and auth refresher lifecycle" with a Colab repro notebook and a short CI plan.

docs-bot: created PR draft on the docs site adding a Notebooks section and examples for Jupyter, Colab, VSCode Interactive.

ci-bot: proposed CI task: run one papermill job on each push that executes the quickstart notebook in headless mode (no heavy model calls — use a local test model stub). Marked as opt-out for forks.

ada: one nit — in Colab the kernel restart semantics differ from local Jupyter; we should add a short paragraph describing what exceptions users might see in each. That helped me differentiate the root cause from unrelated Colab network issues.

chris: for SDK changes I'll open a small PR that: - updates sync helper to check running loop and raise helpful error - defers starting auth refresher until `AsyncClient.__aenter__` or until an internal `.start_refresher(loop=...)` call - adds a `redwood.notebook` convenience shim. I'll include unit tests that assert no tasks remain after simulated loop shutdown.

pat: I'll add the papermill CI job and a mock server to avoid contacting prod. Also will add a tiny e2e that restarts the kernel once to exercise lifecycle.

ada: thanks! ping me on the PR, I'll validate on Colab and VSCode Interactive. :thumbsup:
